original.guitar: Acoustic-driven arrangement with fiddle, banjo and mandolin (session players not credited in the sources found)
original.notes: From True Believers (May 2013), produced by Frank Rogers, recorded at Blackbird Studios, the Pool House and Charleston Sound. Backing vocals by Lady Antebellum.

recipes.tips: The song is built on strummed acoustic guitar. The ACOUSTIC effect in the PEDAL slot makes your electric sound like one. Channel A is warmer, channel B brighter. Strum the four-chord progression with a light, even down-up pattern. Turn PEDAL off for a plain clean electric. For electric fills and licks, switch to WAGON EL.
recipes.why: If there's no acoustic player in the band, an acoustic simulation into a very clean amp covers the song's main part. Split pickups in the middle position give the least electric-sounding source for the simulation.

recipes.tips: Channel A for clean, twangy fills between the vocal lines. Channel B for a warmer, slightly broken-up sound for a solo. Leave room for the fiddle and banjo: short licks, double stops and pedal-steel-style bends work best.
recipes.why: In an acoustic-driven arrangement, the electric guitar plays sparse fills: a clean, lightly compressed Tele sound with a slapback and spring reverb.
